literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 被遣返的居民,经过 42 天的监测,未发现继发 ANDV 感染。此外,来自 33 个国家的约 653 名潜在暴露者在全球范围内接受了评估和监测。 [10.15585/mmwr.mm7543a1]
该研究鉴定了 2026 年 暴发 中 ANDV 分离株的遗传多样性,并提供了对其系统动力学模式的见解,尽管所提供的证据中没有详细说明具体的数值结果。 [10.1080/23744235.2026.2758370]
鉴定出两种结合 Qa-1 的 HTNV 糖蛋白衍生九肽。使用已鉴定的 HTNV 肽进行免疫并随后进行 HTNV 攻击后,野生型 (WT) 小鼠表现出肾脏免疫病理学减弱,而 D227K 敲入小鼠(Qa-1-CD8/TCR 相互作用被破坏)表现出脾脏和肾脏中病毒清除率增强,但肾脏免疫病理学加剧。 [10.1073/pnas.2536836123]
纳入了 63 项研究;24个贡献了2×2数据,22个初步比较进入了主综合。 [10.1016/j.diagmicrobio.2026.117722]
研究报告称,汉坦病毒 主要与啮齿动物有关,可引起严重的人类疾病,包括 HFRS 和 HPS。它还指出,汉坦病毒科包括多个属,其中正汉坦病毒属与人类疾病最相关。 [10.1093/ajrccm/aamag395]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: residents repatriated, no secondary ANDV infections were identified after 42 days of monitoring. Additionally, approximately 653 potentially exposed persons from 33 countries were assessed and monitored globally. [10.15585/mmwr.mm7543a1]

The study identified genetic diversity within ANDV isolates from the 2026 outbreak and provided insights into its phylodynamic patterns, though specific numerical results were not detailed in the supplied evidence. [10.1080/23744235.2026.2758370]
Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. [10.1073/pnas.2536836123]
Sixty-three studies were included; 24 contributed 2 × 2 data and 22 primary comparisons entered the main synthesis. [10.1016/j.diagmicrobio.2026.117722]

The study reports that hantaviruses are primarily associated with rodents and can cause severe human diseases, including HFRS and HPS. It also notes that the Hantaviridae family includes several genera, with orthohantaviruses being the most relevant to human disease. [10.1093/ajrccm/aamag395]

news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 西班牙确认从 MV Hondius 游轮撤离的 14 名西班牙国民中,其中一名汉坦病毒检测结果初步呈阳性。西班牙卫生部长莫妮卡·加西亚表示,该人仍处于隔离状态,并正在接受持续的临床观察。 [news-2d174b89e8477f59]
MV Hondius 号游轮上报告有疑似汉坦病毒暴发 病例,造成 3 人死亡,1 人接受重症监护。世界卫生组织(WHO)确认了两例实验室确诊病例和五例疑似病例,其中死者乘客的妻子汉坦病毒检测呈阳性。世界卫生组织正在开展调查和进一步的实验室测试。 [news-45adf4c479190201]
2018-2019 年阿根廷埃普延发生的汉坦病毒暴发 事件导致 34 例病例和 11 人死亡。幸存者和受害者家属,包括伊莎贝尔·迪亚兹和她的父亲维克多·迪亚兹,被确定为零号病人,并讲述了 暴发 的影响。最近还报道了 MV Hondius 游轮上的汉坦病毒暴发,但细节有限。 [news-1853ee44282cc7c8]
科学家们确定了新世界汉坦病毒(如安第斯病毒)如何识别人类细胞受体原钙粘蛋白-1(PCDH1)进入宿主细胞的结构基础。这是通过对该病毒的结构和功能及其与 PCDH1 的相互作用进行分析来实现的。 [news-ef08c4511943ff97]
汉滩病毒研究表明,受 HLA-E 限制的 CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞在防止肾脏损伤方面发挥双重作用,同时可能延迟病毒清除。这是通过 HFRS 患者的血液样本分析和小鼠模型实验确定的。 [news-58298d76da219f8c]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hantaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: Spain confirmed a preliminary positive Hantavirus test in one of the 14 Spanish nationals evacuated from the MV Hondius cruise ship. The Spanish Health Minister, Monica Garcia, stated that the individual remains in isolation and is under continued clinical observation. [news-2d174b89e8477f59]

A suspected hantavirus outbreak has been reported aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, with three deaths and one person in intensive care. The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases, with the deceased passenger's wife testing positive for hantavirus. [news-45adf4c479190201]

A hantavirus outbreak in Epuyén, Argentina, in 2018-2019 resulted in 34 cases and 11 fatalities. Survivors and family members of the victims, including Isabel Díaz and her father Víctor Díaz, were identified as patient zero and recounted the impact of the outbreak. [news-1853ee44282cc7c8]

Scientists identified the structural basis of how New World hantaviruses, such as Andes virus, recognize the human cell receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells. This was achieved through structural and functional analyses of the virus and its interaction with PCDH1. [news-ef08c4511943ff97]

Hantaan virus research revealed that CD8+ regulatory T cells, restricted by HLA-E, play a dual role in protecting against kidney damage while potentially delaying viral clearance. This was identified through blood sample analysis from HFRS patients and mouse model experiments. [news-58298d76da219f8c]

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of serological, molecular and rapid tests for human hantavirus disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human hantavirus disease is potentially lethal and overlaps clinically with other febrile, renal, and cardiopulmonary syndromes. Diagnostic performance varies by viral species, specimen type, sampling timing, and reference standard. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize and compare the diagnostic accuracy of serologic, molecular, rapid, multiplex, and antigen-detection tests for human hantavirus infection or disease. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261398030). MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through May 20, 2026. Human studies with an eligible index test and verifiable reference standard were included. Diagnostic accuracy data were extracted when possible. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and certainty with GRADE-DTA. Primary meta-analyses used platform-specific univariate logit-scale models; hierarchical bivariate/HSROC sensitivity analyses were performed for eligible strata. RESULTS: Sixty-three studies were included; 24 contributed 2 × 2 data and 22 primary comparisons entered the main synthesis. ELISA/EIA showed sensitivity of 98.0% and specificity of 98.8%, with low certainty. Rapid-format assays showed sensitivity of 97.4% and specificity of 97.2%, also with low certainty. Molecular tests had specificity of 99.5% and sensitivity of 85.6%. Bivariate sensitivity analyses for ELISA/EIA and rapid-format assays produced similar estimates to the primary models. CONCLUSIONS: In the available low-certainty evidence, ELISA/EIA serology is the best-supported platform, but this is not a universal recommendation. Molecular and rapid tests may be useful in specific contexts and require prospective validation.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human hantavirus disease is potentially lethal and overlaps clinically with other febrile, renal, and cardiopulmonary syndromes. Diagnostic performance varies by viral species, specimen type, sampling timing, and reference standard. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize and compare the diagnostic accuracy of serologic, molecular, rapid, multiplex, and antigen-detection tests for human hantavirus infection or disease. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261398030). MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through May 20, 2026. Human studies with an eligible index test and verifiable reference standard were included. Diagnostic accuracy data were extracted when possible. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and certainty with GRADE-DTA. Primary meta-analyses used platform-specific univariate logit-scale models; hierarchical bivariate/HSROC sensitivity analyses were performed for eligible strata. RESULTS: Sixty-three studies were included; 24 contributed 2 × 2 data and 22 primary comparisons entered the main synthesis. ELISA/EIA showed sensitivity of 98.0% and specificity of 98.8%, with low certainty. Rapid-format assays showed sensitivity of 97.4% and specificity of 97.2%, also with low certainty. Molecular tests had specificity of 99.5% and sensitivity of 85.6%. Bivariate sensitivity analyses for ELISA/EIA and rapid-format assays produced similar estimates to the primary models. CONCLUSIONS: In the available low-certainty evidence, ELISA/EIA serology is the best-supported platform, but this is not a universal recommendation. Molecular and rapid tests may be useful in specific contexts and require prospective validation.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了 ANDV 独特的进化和系统动力学特征,强调其持续人传人 传播 的潜力以及进一步研究其 流行病学 的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于了解 ANDV 的遗传和 传播 动态,这对于改善 监测、诊断 以及公众健康对汉坦病毒暴发 的反应至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因缺乏详细的数值结果和具体的统计分析而受到限制,这可能会影响 ANDV 系统动力学得出的结论的强度。

papers.title: CD8 + regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection.
papers.abstract: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8 + T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8 + regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8 + Tregs (CD122 + Eomes + CD49d lo KIR + ), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8 + T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8 + Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8 + Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the dual role of CD8 + regulatory T cells (Tregs) in Hantaan virus (HTNV) infection, focusing on their ability to limit immunopathology while potentially impairing viral clearance. The research characterizes a CD8 + Treg subset restricted by HLA-E in HFRS patients and a murine HTNV infection model. It identifies two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bind Qa-1 and demonstrates that immunization with these peptides reduces renal immunopathology in wild-type mice. However, in D227K knock-in mice with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction, viral clearance is enhanced but renal immunopathology is exacerbated. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs suppress effector CD8 + T cell proliferation through TGF-β secretion. The D227K mutation alters Treg phenotype, with bulk Tregs upregulating inhibitory receptors and TGF-β, while epitope-specific Tregs lose suppressive function and TGF-β production. These findings suggest that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs play a critical role in balancing immunopathology and viral clearance during HTNV infection, offering potential therapeutic insights for HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers. The study's evidence is strong, but limitations include the focus on a specific murine model and the need for further validation in human contexts.

papers.title: Hantavirus Outbreak Caused by Andes Virus Linked to International Cruise Ship Travel - United States, 2026.
papers.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV), the only hantavirus known to be transmitted person-to-person, is endemic to areas of South America and can cause hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, which has a case-fatality rate of approximately 40%. On May 4, 2026, CDC was notified of seven cases of severe acute respiratory illness, including three deaths, among 147 persons aboard a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean; the illnesses were later confirmed to be caused by ANDV. No cases occurred among passengers who were U.S. resident passengers disembarked before ANDV infection was confirmed aboard the ship. On May 10, the remaining 18 U.S. resident passengers were repatriated to the National Quarantine Unit in Omaha, Nebraska, for risk assessment and monitoring, and where optimized advanced care was available, should symptoms develop. health departments monitored 60 additional U.S. residents potentially exposed on flights involving a passenger with symptomatic ANDV infection from the cruise, totaling 88 contacts across 27 jurisdictions. All 88 contacts completed 42 days of monitoring, with no secondary ANDV infections identified. Worldwide, local health authorities assessed and monitored approximately 653 potentially exposed persons from 33 countries. This response highlights the value of rapid coordination among partners to locate and monitor potentially exposed persons during an international outbreak to reduce the risk for ANDV transmission. Prompt notification to public health authorities can facilitate testing, patient care, contact identification, and implementation of measures to limit secondary transmission.

papers.abstract_zh: 安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 是唯一已知可在人与人之间传播的 汉坦病毒,是南美洲地区的地方病,可引起 汉坦病毒肺综合征,病死率约为 40%。2026 年 5 月 4 日,美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 接到通知,大西洋一艘游轮上的 147 人中有 7 例严重急性呼吸道疾病病例,其中 3 例死亡;这些疾病后来被证实是由 ANDV 引起的。在船上确认 ANDV 感染之前下船的美国居民乘客中没有出现病例。5 月 10 日,其余 18 名美国居民乘客被遣返回内布拉斯加州奥马哈的国家检疫中心进行风险评估和监测,如果出现症状,可以在那里获得优化的高级护理。卫生部门监测了另外 60 名可能在航班上接触过的美国居民,其中涉及一名有症状的 ANDV 感染乘客,他们来自 27 个司法管辖区,总共有 88 名接触者。所有 88 名接触者均完成了 42 天的监测,未发现继发 ANDV 感染。在全球范围内,地方卫生当局评估并监测了来自 33 个国家的约 653 名潜在暴露者。这一响应凸显了合作伙伴之间快速协调的价值,以在国际 暴发 期间定位和监测潜在暴露人员,以降低 ANDV 传播 风险。及时通知公共卫生当局可以促进检测、患者护理、接触者识别以及实施限制继发性 传播 的措施。
papers.summary_zh: 安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 是唯一已知可在人与人之间传播的 汉坦病毒,是南美洲地区的地方病,可引起 汉坦病毒肺综合征,病死率约为 40%。2026 年 5 月 4 日,美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 接到通知,大西洋一艘游轮上的 147 人中有 7 例严重急性呼吸道疾病病例,其中 3 例死亡;这些疾病后来被证实是由 ANDV 引起的。在船上确认 ANDV 感染之前下船的美国居民乘客中没有出现病例。5 月 10 日,其余 18 名美国居民乘客被遣返回内布拉斯加州奥马哈的国家检疫中心进行风险评估和监测,如果出现症状,可以在那里获得优化的高级护理。卫生部门监测了另外 60 名可能在航班上接触过的美国居民,其中涉及一名有症状的 ANDV 感染乘客,他们来自 27 个司法管辖区,总共有 88 名接触者。所有 88 名接触者均完成了 42 天的监测,未发现继发 ANDV 感染。在全球范围内,地方卫生当局评估并监测了来自 33 个国家的约 653 名潜在暴露者。这一响应凸显了合作伙伴之间快速协调的价值,以在国际 暴发 期间定位和监测潜在暴露人员,以降低 ANDV 传播 风险。及时通知公共卫生当局可以促进检测、患者护理、接触者识别以及实施限制继发性 传播 的措施。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查国际游轮 暴发 中安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 的 传播 动态,强调了解汉坦病毒人际传播 传播 及其公共卫生影响的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了 2026 年大西洋一艘游轮上发生的 ANDV 暴发,其中 147 名乘客报告了 7 例严重急性呼吸道疾病病例,其中 3 例死亡。暴发 涉及美国居民和其他国际旅行者。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究涉及对潜在接触者的监测和风险评估,其中包括被遣返回内布拉斯加州奥马哈的 18 名美国居民以及 27 个司法管辖区的 88 名接触者。公共卫生当局对所有潜在暴露者进行了评估和监测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 被遣返的居民,经过 42 天的监测,未发现继发 ANDV 感染。此外,来自 33 个国家的约 653 名潜在暴露者在全球范围内接受了评估和监测。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在监测期间,ANDV 并未传播给次要接触者,这表明人与人之间 传播 的风险在某些条件下可能是有限的。这凸显了快速公共卫生反应在控制 暴发 方面的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调了在国际 暴发 期间迅速进行公共卫生协调以识别和监测潜在暴露个体的必要性,这有助于防止 ANDV 进一步 传播。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其观察性质和对报告病例的依赖而受到限制,没有提供详细的统计分析。然而,由于对接触者进行了全面监测并且没有继发感染,证据是有力的。

papers.title: Ecological Correlates and Spatiotemporal Trends of Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome in West Kazakhstan: A 25-Year One Health Surveillance Study (2001–2025)
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a rodent-borne zoonosis of public health concern in West Kazakhstan, yet long-term studies linking human and reservoir surveillance are scarce. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HFRS cases (2001–2025) and routine rodent surveillance data from five districts of the West Kazakhstan Region within a One Health framework. Associations were estimated using negative binomial regression with district fixed effects and year-clustered robust standard errors (2002–2024; 115 district-years). Overall, 314 cases were recorded (81.2% male), with a major outbreak in 2005 (85 cases) and a resurgence in 2024–2025 (27 and 41 cases). Burlinsky District reported the most cases (44.9%), whereas Baiterek District had the highest incidence in 2016–2025. Of 132,694 rodents examined, 1083 (0.82%) were hantavirus antigen-positive. A larger share of the annual Mus musculus catch obtained in spring–summer was associated with higher case counts (incidence rate ratio 1.051 per percentage point; 95% CI: 1.024–1.080), and this was robust to excluding outbreak years. The number of positive rodents was associated with cases, but not after standardization for sampling effort. These associations do not establish M. musculus as a reservoir and are consistent with, but do not demonstrate, increased peridomestic exposure.

We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HFRS cases (2001–2025) and routine rodent surveillance data from five districts of the West Kazakhstan Region within a One Health framework. Associations were estimated using negative binomial regression with district fixed effects and year-clustered robust standard errors (2002–2024; 115 district-years). Overall, 314 cases were recorded (81.2% male), with a major outbreak in 2005 (85 cases) and a resurgence in 2024–2025 (27 and 41 cases). Burlinsky District reported the most cases (44.9%), whereas Baiterek District had the highest incidence in 2016–2025. Of 132,694 rodents examined, 1083 (0.82%) were hantavirus antigen-positive. A larger share of the annual Mus musculus catch obtained in spring–summer was associated with higher case counts (incidence rate ratio 1.051 per percentage point; 95% CI: 1.024–1.080), and this was robust to excluding outbreak years. The number of positive rodents was associated with cases, but not after standardization for sampling effort. These associations do not establish M. musculus as a reservoir and are consistent with, but do not demonstrate, increased peridomestic exposure.

papers.title: Dinámica de la Información Digital en español ante un riesgo emergente de salud pública: análisis exploratorio del caso hantavirus
papers.abstract: Este artículo analiza la dinámica temporal de la información digital en español relacionada con el hantavirus como caso de un riesgo emergente de salud pública. Se realizó un estudio observacional, retrospectivo, descriptivo y exploratorio a partir de publicaciones digitales recuperadas mediante un canal de monitoreo orientado a México. De las 1,054 publicaciones en español recuperadas, 899 conformaron el corpus final, correspondiente al periodo del 7 de mayo al 8 de agosto de 2026. La delimitación temporal y la exclusión de registros sin fecha válida definieron esta selección. El volumen de publicaciones se analizó por día y los periodos de mayor actividad se identificaron a partir de la media y la desviación estándar. Se observaron tres episodios principales, con máximos de 78, 139 y 169 publicaciones. Los seis días clasificados como de alta actividad reunieron el 71.5% del corpus. El mayor volumen se registró el 19 de mayo, fecha en la que predominaron los contenidos relacionados con vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica (41.4%). La actividad informativa mostró una clara concentración temporal y una composición distinta entre episodios. Estos patrones permiten caracterizar cómo evolucionó el entorno informativo ante acontecimientos de interés para la salud pública. El volumen de publicaciones, sin embargo, no representa una medida de intensidad epidemiológica.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the temporal dynamics of digital information in Spanish related to hantavirus as an emerging public health risk. It conducted an observational, retrospective, descriptive, and exploratory analysis of 899 Spanish-language publications retrieved through a monitoring channel focused on Mexico, spanning May 7 to August 8, 2026. The research identified three main periods of activity, with peaks of 78, 139, and 169 publications, and found that six high-activity days accounted for 71.5% of the corpus. The highest volume of publications was recorded on May 19, where content related to surveillance or epidemiological research dominated at 41.4%. These patterns highlight how the information environment evolves in response to public health events. However, the study notes that publication volume does not equate to epidemiological intensity. The findings offer insights into digital information dynamics during health emergencies but are limited by the temporal scope and the absence of direct epidemiological measures.

papers.title: Đặc điểm dịch tễ học các ca nhiễm Hantavirus ở người và tình trạng nhiễm trên chuột tại địa điểm có ca bệnh, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, 2012 – 2014: Báo cáo loạt ca
papers.abstract: Nghiên cứu hồi cứu này nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ các trường hợp nhiễm Hantavirus ở người và xácđịnh tỷ lệ mẫu huyết thanh chuột dương tính với Hantavirus tại các địa điểm ghi nhận ca bệnh ở Thànhphố Hồ Chí Minh giai đoạn 2012–2014. Dữ liệu được thu thập từ hệ thống giám sát bệnh truyền nhiễm củaViện Pasteur Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh. Kết quả ghi nhận 6 ca nhiễm Hantavirus ở người, không có tử vong.Năm 2014 có số ca cao nhất với 3 ca (50,0%); nam giới chiếm 83,3% và phần lớn ca bệnh trên 30 tuổi.Tất cả đều tăng creatinine huyết thanh (173–671 μmol/L), trong đó 4 ca giảm tiểu cầu (11.000–58.000 tếbào/mm3); tất cả đều hồi phục sau điều trị. Chuột và chất thải chuột được ghi nhận tại nơi sinh sống của tấtcả bệnh nhân. Trong 309 mẫu huyết thanh chuột được xét nghiệm, có 88 mẫu dương tính với Hantavirus(28,5%); tỷ trọng mẫu dương tính cao nhất được ghi nhận ở chuột cống (Rattus norvegicus) (87,5%). Kếtquả cho thấy Hantavirus lưu hành trong quần thể chuột tại các địa điểm ghi nhận ca bệnh, tiềm ẩn nguycơ phơi nhiễm ở người trong môi trường đô thị. Cần tăng cường giám sát ca bệnh, năng lực xét nghiệmHantavirus và giám sát định kỳ trên chuột nhằm hỗ trợ phát hiện sớm và triển khai các biện pháp phòng,chống kịp thời.

Kết quả ghi nhận 6 ca nhiễm Hantavirus ở người, không có tử vong.Năm 2014 có số ca cao nhất với 3 ca (50,0%); nam giới chiếm 83,3% và phần lớn ca bệnh trên 30 tuổi.Tất cả đều tăng creatinine huyết thanh (173–671 μmol/L), trong đó 4 ca giảm tiểu cầu (11.000–58.000 tếbào/mm3); tất cả đều hồi phục sau điều trị. papers.title: The origin of the MV Hondius Andes outbreak
papers.abstract: In April-July 2026, Andes virus (ANDV) caused an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulting in 12 confirmed cases and three deaths. Before symptom onset, the index case had travelled through hantavirus-endemic regions of Chile and Argentina, leaving the geographic origin of infection unresolved. We conducted phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses using newly generated ANDV genomes from human cases and rodent reservoirs to investigate the likely origin of the outbreak. Through phylogenetic analyses, we show that the outbreak genome falls within a geographically structured lineage spanning southern Chile and Argentine Andean Patagonia. Using phylogeographic reconstructions across all three segments, integrated with the index case's travel itinerary, we identified the Toltén-Lanco area of southern Chile as the most likely geographic origin of the outbreak genome, with two candidate locations accounting for >98% of the posterior support. However, the index case visited this area 62-66 days before symptom onset, exceeding the conventionally reported ANDV incubation period of 7-42 days. Thus, while genomic evidence supports a southern Chilean origin of the outbreak genome, the timing and circumstances of transmission to the index case remain unresolved.

The index case had previously traveled through hantavirus-endemic regions of Chile and Argentina, but the exact geographic origin of infection remained unresolved.
analysis.methods: Phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses were performed using newly generated ANDV genomes from human cases and rodent reservoirs to trace the likely origin of the outbreak.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the outbreak likely originated from southern Chile, but the timing of the index case's travel to this area exceeds the conventionally reported ANDV incubation period, raising questions about the transmission dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical insights into the geographic spread of ANDV and highlight the need for targeted surveillance in southern Chile to prevent future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's confidence is moderate due to the uncertainty surrounding the timing of the index case's exposure, which exceeds the conventional incubation period, and the reliance on genomic data without direct epidemiological confirmation.

The findings suggest the need for enhanced surveillance in southern Chile to prevent future outbreaks, but the evidence is limited by the uncertainty in the index case's exposure timing and the absence of direct epidemiological confirmation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定 2026 年 4 月至 7 月 MV Hondius 游轮上安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 暴发 的地理起源,该游轮导致 12 例确诊病例和 3 人死亡。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2026 年 4 月至 7 月在 MV Hondius 游轮上进行,涉及 12 例确诊的 ANDV 感染人类病例,其中 3 例死亡。该指示病例此前曾去过智利和阿根廷汉坦病毒流行地区,但感染的确切地理来源仍未确定。
elements_zh.methods: 使用从人类病例和啮齿动物 储存宿主 中新生成的 ANDV 基因组 进行系统发育和系统发育地理学分析,以追踪 暴发 的可能起源。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析表明,暴发 基因组 属于跨越智利南部和阿根廷安第斯巴塔哥尼亚的地理结构谱系。最可能的起源被确定为智利南部的托尔滕-兰科地区,两个候选位置占后部支撑的 98% 以上。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,暴发 可能起源于智利南部,但指示病例前往该地区的时间超过了传统报告的 ANDV 潜伏期,这引发了对 传播 动态的质疑。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为了解 ANDV 的地理传播提供了重要见解,并强调需要在智利南部制定针对性的 监测 以预防未来的 暴发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的置信度为中等,因为指示病例的暴露时间存在不确定性,超过了传统的潜伏期,并且依赖于基因组数据而没有直接的流行病学确认。

papers.title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), particularly mammalian orthohantaviruses associated with human disease and their specific syndromes. The central question is how to safely move such patients between the community, hospitals, and high-level isolation units, emphasizing the integration of biosafety science and emergency medicine.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and organized across seven operational domains, incorporating the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies, and the findings are primarily based on case reports and technical evaluations. There is limited evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions, and the framework components require prospective evaluation. Additionally, the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service is a key contributor to the framework, but this may not be universally applicable.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The proposed framework serves as a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance in biocontainment transport. It highlights the need for prospective evaluation of its components and emphasizes the importance of integrating biosafety science with emergency medical systems to improve patient transport safety for HCIDs.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases, particularly mammalian orthohantaviruses, emphasizing the integration of biosafety science and emergency medicine. The evidence base includes a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus, guided by international health organizations, and operational experience from the Italian Red Cross. Key findings highlight recurring challenges such as device integrity, self-contamination risks, heat strain, and communication limitations during transport. These are synthesized into a framework with four containment links, seven operational phases, three complexity tiers, and a role-based matrix. The review identifies a lack of comparative studies and calls for prospective evaluation of the framework. It underscores the need for improved planning, training, and quality assurance in biocontainment transport systems to ensure safe patient movement for HCIDs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是患有严重后果传染病(HCID)的患者的运输,特别是与人类疾病及其特定综合征相关的哺乳动物正汉坦病毒。核心问题是如何在社区、医院和高级隔离单位之间安全转移此类患者,强调生物安全科学与急救医学的结合。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日的 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 进行了结构化检索,并得到了世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导。调查结果根据 SANRA 规模进行报告,并跨七个业务领域进行组织,结合了意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估、专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果包括运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、热应变、个人防护设备造成的通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间的团队准备情况以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 文献缺乏比较研究,研究结果主要基于病例报告和技术评估。关于具体干预措施有效性的证据有限,框架组成部分需要前瞻性评估。此外,审查指出,意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验是该框架的关键贡献者,但这可能并不普遍适用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 拟议的框架为生物防护运输的规划、培训和质量保证提供了结构化、基于共识的参考。它强调了对其组成部分进行前瞻性评估的必要性,并强调了将生物安全科学与紧急医疗系统相结合以提高 HCID 患者运输安全的重要性。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:严重传染病(HCID)患者的转运将生物安全科学和急诊医学联系在一起。2026年的本迪布焦病毒病疫情以及与一艘探险游轮相关的多国安第斯山脉病毒暴发再次引起人们对如何在社区、医院和高级隔离单位之间安全转移此类患者的关注。这篇叙述性综述综合了有关生物防护运输的国际文献,并将其整合到紧急医疗系统的操作框架中。方法:根据 SANRA 量表,对 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus(截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日)进行结构化检索,并辅以世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导。证据跨七个业务领域进行组织,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。结果:在已识别的 2432 条记录中,筛选出 1485 条独特记录。文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估和专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果涉及运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、个人防护设备造成的热应变和通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间团队准备状态的保持以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。结论:生物防护运输最好理解为一个综合应急系统,而不是一种以设备为中心的干预措施。拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考;其组成部分需要前瞻性评估。

papers.title: IDENTIFICATION OF A STRUCTURALLY AND EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED 3'→5' PROOFREADING EXONUCLEASE DOMAIN IN THE LARGE L PROTEIN OF HANTAVIRUSES- EMERGING HUMAN PATHOGENS
papers.abstract: The proofreading 3′→5′ exonuclease not only represents a crucial class of enzymes responsible for maintaining genome integrity across diverse groups of organisms, but also plays a critical role in ensuring replication fidelity. In the non-segmented, positive-strand bat-borne RNA viruses like Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronaviruses (SARS-CoVs and MERS-CoV), it is found along with the methyltransferase (MTase) gene of the non-structural protein 14 (NSP14). In contrast, in the non-segmented, but negative-strand bat-borne RNA viruses such as Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses, it has been identified together with a novel type of capping enzyme, viz. guanosine diphosphate polyribonucleotidyltransferase (PRNTase). Hantaviruses, one of the fatal and emerging human pathogens in recent times, belong to segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and are primarily rodent-borne. Currently, no universally approved vaccine or antiviral therapy exists for all hantavirus infections. The presence of a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain has not been reported in hantaviruses until now. Interestingly, a putative PR exonuclease domain has been identified for the first time in these viruses within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The newly identified domain belongs to the DEDD superfamily, but exhibits a distinct structural deviation, notably the replacement of the first catalytic triad -DxE- in the Old World hantaviruses with an -NxE- motif in most of the New World hantaviruses, and the use of an invariant tyrosine instead of histidine at the proton acceptor site. This feature closely resembles the DEDD superfamily of PR exonucleases reported in bacterial DNA polymerases I and II and in the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases of DNA viruses. To the best of my knowledge, this study provides the first evidence for the presence of a typical DEDD superfamily of PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, and thus, expanding our understanding of the structure and catalytic mechanism of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and further presenting a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify a structurally and evolutionarily conserved 3′→5′ proofreading exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, which are emerging human pathogens. The background highlights the importance of such enzymes in maintaining genome integrity and replication fidelity across various organisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on hantaviruses, which are segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses primarily rodent-borne. It examined the presence of a proofreading exonuclease domain in these viruses, particularly within the large L protein, and compared it with other RNA viruses.
analysis.methods: The researchers identified a putative PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses through sequence analysis and structural comparisons. They examined the domain's characteristics, including its catalytic triad and proton acceptor site, and compared it with known DEDD superfamily members in bacterial DNA polymerases and DNA viruses.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that a proofreading exonuclease domain has not been previously identified in hantaviruses. It was found within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), and exhibits a distinct structural deviation, such as the replacement of the -DxE- motif with -NxE- in New World hantaviruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that this study provides the first evidence of a typical DEDD superfamily of PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, which expands our understanding of the structure and catalytic mechanism of these enzymes in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections, which could have significant implications for treatment and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on sequence analysis and structural comparisons, which may not fully capture functional or biochemical evidence. However, the evidence is grounded in the direct identification of the PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies a structurally and evolutionarily conserved 3′→5′ proofreading exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, which are emerging human pathogens. The research highlights the absence of such a domain in hantaviruses until now and reveals its presence within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The domain exhibits a distinct structural deviation, such as the replacement of the -DxE- motif with -NxE- in New World hantaviruses. The authors interpret this as the first evidence of a DEDD superfamily PR exonuclease in hantaviruses, expanding our understanding of these enzymes in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses. The findings suggest a potential novel structural target for antiviral therapies against hantavirus infections. However, the study is based on sequence analysis and structural comparisons, which may limit the confidence in its conclusions. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the absence of direct biochemical or functional validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在鉴定 汉坦病毒(新兴的人类病原体)中结构和进化上保守的 3′→5′ 校对核酸外切酶结构域。背景强调了此类酶在维持各种生物体中 基因组 完整性和复制保真度方面的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究的重点是 汉坦病毒,这是一种主要由啮齿动物传播的分段负链 RNA 病毒。它检查了这些病毒中是否存在校对核酸外切酶结构域,特别是在大 L 蛋白内,并将其与其他 RNA 病毒进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过序列分析和结构比较,在汉坦病毒中鉴定出了一个假定的 PR 核酸外切酶结构域。他们检查了该结构域的特征,包括其催化三联体和质子受体位点,并将其与细菌 DNA 聚合酶和 DNA 病毒中已知的 DEDD 超家族成员进行了比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,此前尚未在汉坦病毒中鉴定出校对核酸外切酶结构域。它是在大 L 蛋白中发现的,位于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 之前,并表现出明显的结构偏差,例如在 New World汉坦病毒中用 -NxE- 替换 -DxE- 基序。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这项研究提供了汉坦病毒中 PR 核酸外切酶结构域的典型 DEDD 超家族的第一个证据,这扩展了我们对分段负链 RNA 病毒中这些酶的结构和催化机制的理解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为开发针对致命性汉坦病毒感染的普遍有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法提供了一个新的结构目标,这可能对 治疗 和预防策略产生重大影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于序列分析和结构比较,可能无法完全捕获功能或生化证据。然而,证据基于汉坦病毒中 PR 核酸外切酶结构域的直接识别,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.abstract_zh: 校对 3′→5′ 核酸外切酶不仅代表了一类关键的酶,负责在不同生物体群体中维持 基因组 的完整性,而且在确保复制保真度方面也发挥着关键作用。在非节段、正链蝙蝠传播的 RNA 病毒中,如严重急性呼吸系统综合症冠状病毒(SARS-CoV 和 MERS-CoV),它与非结构蛋白 14 (NSP14) 的甲基转移酶 (MTase) 基因一起被发现。相比之下,在马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和尼帕病毒等不分节但负链的蝙蝠传播RNA病毒中,它与一种新型加帽酶一起被鉴定出来,即加帽酶。二磷酸鸟苷多聚核糖核苷酸转移酶(PRNTase)。汉坦病毒是近年来新出现的致命人类病原体之一,属于分段负链RNA病毒,主要由啮齿类动物传播。目前,尚无针对所有汉坦病毒感染的普遍批准的 疫苗 或 抗病毒药物 疗法。迄今为止,汉坦病毒 中尚未报道校对 (PR) 核酸外切酶结构域的存在。有趣的是,首次在这些病毒的大 L 蛋白中发现了一个推定的 PR 核酸外切酶结构域,位于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 之前。新鉴定的结构域属于DEDD超家族,但表现出明显的结构偏差,特别是旧世界汉坦病毒中的第一个催化三联体-DxE-被大多数新世界汉坦病毒中的-NxE-基序取代,以及在质子受体位点使用不变的酪氨酸代替组氨酸。这一特征与细菌 DNA 聚合酶 I 和 II 以及 DNA 病毒的 DNA 依赖性 DNA 聚合酶中报道的 PR 核酸外切酶 DEDD 超家族非常相似。据我所知,这项研究为汉坦病毒中PR外切核酸酶结构域的典型DEDD超家族的存在提供了第一个证据,从而扩大了我们对分段负链RNA病毒中3′→5′PR外切核酸酶的结构和催化机制的理解,并进一步为开发针对致命性汉坦病毒感染的普遍有效的抗病毒药物疗法提供了一个新的结构靶点。

papers.title: Time‐dependent sensitivity of R0 and other threshold parameters in seasonal ecological and epidemiological dynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract Periodically driven systems are ubiquitous in nature, and their stability against perturbations such as the introduction of a novel pathogens or invasive species is often a major concern. To better understand and control these systems, it is common to assess the sensitivity to changes in the model parameters of stability threshold quantities such as the basic reproduction number , or the Floquet multiplier , which determines stability against invasion of the disease/invader‐free system. However, traditional methods often assume that these parameter changes are permanent and constant in time, so they may over‐ or underpredict the cost‐effectiveness of management activities that can only be maintained for a limited time during each period, such as culling when most individuals are at an especially vulnerable life‐stage. Moreover, they cannot highlight important time junctures in the model dynamics. In this article, we address this problem by providing efficient algorithms to compute the sensitivities of objectives like and to periodic, time‐localised perturbations in the model parameters. These sensitivities provide information about when during each period interventions should have the largest effect on the objective, and can also be used to calculate the sensitivities to more general periodic perturbations. Hence, this article extends previous work on time‐dependent sensitivity analysis (TDSA) to a new class of problems relevant to stability analysis. Using empirically parameterised models for Lyme disease and hantavirus, we demonstrate that TDSA can provide useful and sometimes surprising insights that nonetheless have intuitive biological interpretations. Specifically, we find that culling at the optimal times of susceptible and infected non‐human hosts has additive effects in the hantavirus model, but opposite and nearly cancelling effects in the Lyme disease model, so that indiscriminate culling is predicted to be effective for hantavirus but ineffective for Lyme disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional methods in assessing the sensitivity of stability threshold quantities to time-dependent perturbations, which are critical for understanding the dynamics of diseases like hantavirus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used empirically parameterised models for Lyme disease and hantavirus to demonstrate the application of time-dependent sensitivity analysis (TDSA) in evaluating the impact of interventions over time.
analysis.methods: The authors developed efficient algorithms to compute the sensitivities of objectives like R0 to periodic, time-localised perturbations in model parameters, enabling the analysis of interventions at specific times during each period.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that culling at optimal times of susceptible and infected non-human hosts has additive effects in the hantavirus model, but opposite and nearly cancelling effects in the Lyme disease model.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating that TDSA can provide useful and sometimes surprising insights with intuitive biological explanations, extending previous work on time-dependent sensitivity analysis to new problems relevant to stability analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the timing of interventions for hantavirus, such as culling, to maximise their effectiveness, while highlighting the need for caution in applying similar strategies to Lyme disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on model-based simulations, which may not fully capture real-world complexities, and the results are specific to the parameterised models used, limiting generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces time-dependent sensitivity analysis (TDSA) to evaluate the impact of interventions on stability threshold quantities like R0 in periodic ecological and epidemiological systems. Using models for hantavirus and Lyme disease, the authors demonstrate that TDSA can reveal how interventions affect disease dynamics over time. They find that culling at optimal times of susceptible and infected non-human hosts has additive effects in the hantavirus model but opposite and nearly cancelling effects in the Lyme disease model. This suggests that indiscriminate culling may be effective for hantavirus but not for Lyme disease. The study extends previous work on TDSA and highlights its potential for informing targeted management strategies. However, the results are based on model simulations, which may not fully reflect real-world complexities, and the findings are specific to the parameterised models used, limiting generalisability. The evidence is considered moderate due to these limitations.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用莱姆病和汉坦病毒的经验参数化模型来证明时间依赖性敏感性分析 (TDSA) 在评估干预措施随时间的影响方面的应用。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明 TDSA 可以通过直观的生物学解释提供有用的、有时令人惊讶的见解,将之前的时间依赖性敏感性分析工作扩展到与稳定性分析相关的新问题。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 周期性驱动系统在自然界中普遍存在,其针对新病原体或入侵物种引入等扰动的稳定性往往是一个主要问题。为了更好地理解和控制这些系统,通常评估稳定性阈值量模型参数变化的敏感性,例如基本繁殖数或 Floquet 乘数,它决定了针对疾病/无入侵者系统入侵的稳定性。然而,传统方法通常假设这些参数变化是永久性的且随时间变化的,因此它们可能高估或低估了只能在每个时期内维持有限时间的管理活动的成本效益,例如当大多数个体处于特别脆弱的生命阶段时的扑杀。此外,它们无法突出模型动态中的重要时间节点。在本文中,我们通过提供有效的算法来计算目标的敏感性(例如模型参数中的周期性、时间局部扰动)来解决这个问题。这些敏感性提供了有关每个时期干预措施何时对目标产生最大影响的信息,并且还可用于计算对更一般的周期性扰动的敏感性。因此,本文将之前关于时间相关敏感性分析(TDSA)的工作扩展到与稳定性分析相关的一类新问题。使用莱姆病和汉坦病毒的经验参数化模型,我们证明 TDSA 可以提供有用的、有时令人惊讶的见解,但仍然具有直观的生物学解释。具体来说,我们发现在易感和受感染的非人类 宿主 的最佳时间进行扑杀在汉坦病毒模型中具有相加效应,但在莱姆病模型中具有相反且几乎抵消的效果,因此预测不加区别的扑杀对汉坦病毒有效,但对莱姆病无效。

news.content: Feedback | Friday, November 06, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Spain Confirms Preliminary Positive Hantavirus Test in MV Hondius Evacuee 12/05/26 | 10:26 am | Hantavirus Test | Positive Hantavirus Test | Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Spain Confirms Preliminary Positive Hantavirus Test in MV Hondius Evacuee Representational photo (Source: Xinhua/IANS) One of the 14 Spanish nationals evacuated from the hantavirus-hit cruise ship MV Hondius has preliminarily tested positive for the virus, Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia said on Sunday. Garcia wrote on X on Monday (local time) that one of the Spanish passengers currently under isolation at Madrid’s Gomez Ulla hospital had tested preliminarily positive in a PCR test conducted upon arrival. “The person remains in isolation, without symptoms and in general good health, under continued clinical observation in accordance with established safety and epidemiological protocols,” she wrote. The other 13 Spaniards tested provisionally negative, while final results were expected in the coming hours, the minister said. According to health authorities and the World Health Organization (WHO), the outbreak is believed to involve the Andes strain of hantavirus, a variant known for possible person-to-person transmission through close contact. The virus is typically transmitted through exposure to infected rodent urine or droppings. The Spanish evacuees were transferred to Madrid as part of an evacuation operation launched after the MV Hondius arrived in Spain’s Canary Islands over the weekend, reports Xinhua news agency. Multiple confirmed and suspected cases have so far been linked to the outbreak, including passengers transferred to several countries for treatment and monitoring. The final group of evacuees left the ship on Monday after the vessel briefly docked at the Port of Granadilla on the Spanish island of Tenerife due to adverse weather conditions. The ship later departed for Rotterdam in the Netherlands. Meanwhile, the European Commission said Monday that it is coordinating and supporting national authorities’ response to a hantavirus outbreak, while the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) assesses the risk to the general population in Europe as very low. Since Spain activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism on May 6, the EU’s Emergency Response Coordination Centre has been facilitating the safe evacuation of people aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship, which was anchored off Tenerife. Five repatriation flights coordinated by the EU took place on Sunday and were carried out by France, Spain, the Netherlands, Greece and Ireland. A sixth and final flight, operated by the Netherlands, departed on Monday, according to the Commission. The EU is also mobilising response capabilities and stockpiles from its strategic reserve. A medical evacuation aircraft from the EU fleet, hosted by Norway, has been pre-positioned in Tenerife, while additional transport and logistics capacities, as well as protective equipment, are ready to be deployed if needed. The Emergency Response Coordination Centre has deployed a liaison officer to Tenerife to support on-site coordination with relevant authorities. The ECDC also deployed two experts from the EU Health Task Force to the ship before passengers disembarked. According to the Commission, the EU is working closely with EU members, countries participating in the Civil Protection Mechanism, the ECDC, the World Health Organization and G7 partners in responding to the outbreak. Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib, said health threats can easily cross borders and coordination is therefore essential. analysis.time: The Spanish Health Minister announced the preliminary positive Hantavirus test on Sunday, November 03, 2026. The final results were expected in the coming hours. The evacuation operation was launched after the MV Hondius arrived in Spain’s Canary Islands over the weekend, and the final group of evacuees left the ship on Monday.
analysis.location_and_population: The event occurred on the cruise ship MV Hondius, which was anchored off Tenerife, Spain. The affected population includes 14 Spanish nationals evacuated from the ship, with one preliminarily testing positive for Hantavirus. The other 13 tested provisionally negative.
analysis.event: Spain confirmed a preliminary positive Hantavirus test in one of the 14 Spanish nationals evacuated from the MV Hondius cruise ship. The Spanish Health Minister, Monica Garcia, stated that the individual remains in isolation and is under continued clinical observation.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak is believed to involve the Andes strain of Hantavirus, which is known for possible person-to-person transmission through close contact. The European Commission and ECDC have coordinated the response and assessed the risk to the general population in Europe as very low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Spanish Health Minister confirmed the preliminary positive test and stated that the individual is under isolation and clinical observation. OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM Share Follow ABC News on Google A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." Popular Reads Captain identified after deadly Florida Learjet crash Nov 3 NYC Marathon runner, 24, dies after developing rhabdomyolysis midrace Nov 3 Learjet with 9 aboard crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida: FAA Nov 1 WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus said in a post on X on Sunday that the organization is working closely with both member states and ship operators in response to the suspected hantavirus cases. "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC. OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM Share Follow ABC News on Google A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." Popular Reads Captain identified after deadly Florida Learjet crash Nov 3 NYC Marathon runner, 24, dies after developing rhabdomyolysis midrace Nov 3 Learjet with 9 aboard crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida: FAA Nov 1 WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus said in a post on X on Sunday that the organization is working closely with both member states and ship operators in response to the suspected hantavirus cases. "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC. news.content_title: Hantavirus outbreak renews painful memories for Patagonian village
news.content: Thursday, November 5, 2026 Argentina Economy Latin America World Culture Sports Opinion ARGENTINA | 11-05-2026 13:46 Hantavirus outbreak renews painful memories for Patagonian village A 2018 outbreak of hantavirus in the small Patagonian town of Epuyén led to 34 cases and 11 fatalities. James Grainger Editor-in-Chief, Buenos Aires Times. Share this News Hantavirus disease survivors Isabel Díaz (left) and her father Víctor Díaz, identified by health authorities as patient zero during the 2018-2019 outbreak that killed 11 people, including her mother and his wife, pose at their farm in the La Rinconada area, near Epuyén, Chubut Province, Argentina, on May 9, 2026. | JUAN MABROMATA / AFP Mailen Valle lost her father and two sisters during a hantavirus outbreak more than seven years ago in Epuyén, a village in Argentina's Patagonia region. With the recent hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship, hard memories have resurfaced for the 33-year-old. "Losing my dad and my two sisters in less than a month..." she told AFP, trailing off. Her voice broke and she laughed nervously, opting to read from a prepared statement because she knew it would be hard to speak. Read more... news.content_title: Hantaan Virus Reveals Immune System Trade-Off
news.content: HANTAAN virus research reveals how regulatory immune cells protect against kidney damage while potentially delaying viral clearance . New findings highlight a complex relationship between antiviral immunity and tissue injury in hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), identifying CD8+ regulatory T cells as potential targets for future therapeutic strategies. Hantaan virus infection can cause HFRS, a potentially severe condition characterized by renal injury and immune dysfunction. Although virus-specific CD8+ T cells contribute to viral elimination, their activity can also trigger damaging inflammatory responses. Researchers investigated a subset of CD8+ regulatory T cells restricted by the immune recognition molecule HLA-E, examining their characteristics in patients with HFRS and their function in a mouse model of infection. Blood samples from patients with HFRS revealed significantly reduced levels of these regulatory T cells. The remaining cells exhibited features of terminal differentiation, including increased expression of inhibitory and regulatory markers KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L. These changes correlated with disease severity, suggesting that altered immune regulation may contribute to more severe Hantaan virus infection. To investigate the mechanisms underlying these findings, researchers identified two Hantaan virus glycoprotein peptides capable of binding Qa-1, the mouse equivalent of HLA-E. Following peptide immunization and subsequent viral challenge, wild-type mice demonstrated reduced renal immunopathology. However, genetically modified mice with disrupted Qa-1 interactions showed improved viral clearance in the kidneys and spleen but experienced more severe renal tissue damage. The findings demonstrate that regulatory immune responses can protect against inflammatory injury while simultaneously restricting the body’s ability to eliminate infection. Further experiments showed that Qa-1-restricted CD8+ regulatory T cells suppressed the proliferation of antiviral effector T cells through peptide-specific interactions and increased transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) secretion. Disrupting these interactions impaired antigen-specific immune suppression, despite compensatory increases in inhibitory markers among the broader regulatory T cell population. The findings identify the HLA-E/CD8+ regulatory T cell pathway as a potential target for host-directed therapies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers. However, therapeutic strategies would need to balance the benefits of limiting inflammatory kidney damage against the potential consequences of delayed viral clearance. Further investigation is required to determine whether manipulating this pathway can improve clinical outcomes in patients. Reference Tang K et al. CD8+ regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2026;123(45):e2536836123. Featured Image: chokniti on Adobe Stock

news.content_original: HANTAAN virus research reveals how regulatory immune cells protect against kidney damage while potentially delaying viral clearance . New findings highlight a complex relationship between antiviral immunity and tissue injury in hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), identifying CD8+ regulatory T cells as potential targets for future therapeutic strategies. Hantaan virus infection can cause HFRS, a potentially severe condition characterized by renal injury and immune dysfunction. Although virus-specific CD8+ T cells contribute to viral elimination, their activity can also trigger damaging inflammatory responses. Researchers investigated a subset of CD8+ regulatory T cells restricted by the immune recognition molecule HLA-E, examining their characteristics in patients with HFRS and their function in a mouse model of infection. Blood samples from patients with HFRS revealed significantly reduced levels of these regulatory T cells. The remaining cells exhibited features of terminal differentiation, including increased expression of inhibitory and regulatory markers KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L. These changes correlated with disease severity, suggesting that altered immune regulation may contribute to more severe Hantaan virus infection. To investigate the mechanisms underlying these findings, researchers identified two Hantaan virus glycoprotein peptides capable of binding Qa-1, the mouse equivalent of HLA-E. Following peptide immunization and subsequent viral challenge, wild-type mice demonstrated reduced renal immunopathology. However, genetically modified mice with disrupted Qa-1 interactions showed improved viral clearance in the kidneys and spleen but experienced more severe renal tissue damage. The findings demonstrate that regulatory immune responses can protect against inflammatory injury while simultaneously restricting the body’s ability to eliminate infection. Further experiments showed that Qa-1-restricted CD8+ regulatory T cells suppressed the proliferation of antiviral effector T cells through peptide-specific interactions and increased transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) secretion. Disrupting these interactions impaired antigen-specific immune suppression, despite compensatory increases in inhibitory markers among the broader regulatory T cell population. The findings identify the HLA-E/CD8+ regulatory T cell pathway as a potential target for host-directed therapies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers. However, therapeutic strategies would need to balance the benefits of limiting inflammatory kidney damage against the potential consequences of delayed viral clearance. Further investigation is required to determine whether manipulating this pathway can improve clinical outcomes in patients. Reference Tang K et al. CD8+ regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2026;123(45):e2536836123. Featured Image: chokniti on Adobe Stock

analysis.brief_en: A recent study published on November 3, 2026, by EMJ explores the dual role of CD8+ regulatory T cells in Hantaan virus infection. These cells, restricted by HLA-E, were found to protect against kidney damage in patients with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) but may also delay viral clearance. Blood samples from HFRS patients showed reduced levels of these cells, which exhibited features of terminal differentiation, including increased expression of inhibitory markers. In mouse models, disrupting Qa-1 interactions led to improved viral clearance but increased renal tissue damage. The findings highlight the need for further research to determine if targeting this pathway could enhance clinical outcomes while balancing the risks of inflammation and delayed viral elimination. The study, titled 'Hantaan Virus Reveals Immune System Trade-Off,' was conducted by researchers at the National Institutes of Health and published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

news.content_zh: EMJ 于 2026 年 11 月 3 日发表的一项最新研究探讨了 CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞在汉坦病毒感染中的双重作用。这些受 HLA-E 限制的细胞被发现可以保护 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 患者免受肾脏损伤,但也可能延迟病毒清除。HFRS 患者的血液样本显示这些细胞水平降低,表现出终末分化的特征,包括抑制标记表达增加。在小鼠模型中,破坏 Qa-1 相互作用可以提高病毒清除率,但会增加肾组织损伤。这些发现强调需要进一步研究,以确定针对这一途径是否可以增强临床结果,同时平衡炎症和延迟病毒消除的风险。这项名为“汉坦病毒揭示免疫系统权衡”的研究由美国国立卫生研究院的研究人员进行,并发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。
