news.content: Subscription Newsletters Photobank Ukrinform - Ukrainian National News Agency Founded in 1918 Friday, 06 November 2026, 05:32 War Economy Sports More ☰ Contacts Eng Укр Eng Esp Deu عربي Fra 日本語 Pol × All topics War Recovery of Ukraine Politics Economy Fact checks Defense Society and Culture Sports Crime Accidents and Emergencies Agency Information on Agency Our Contacts Subscribtion Terms Our Services Privacy policy and personal data protection Additional Publications Interviews Photo Video Longreads Releases Services Subscription Newsletters Photobank War Recovery of Ukraine Politics Economy Fact checks Defense Society and Culture Sports Crime Accidents and Emergencies Publications Interviews Photo Video Longreads Releases Contacts More » Ukraine records dozens of hantavirus cases each year – Public Health Center 11.05.2026 04:30 Ukrinform Ukraine records dozens of hantavirus infection cases every year, with the virus transmitted from rodents to humans. Mykola Hanich, spokesperson for the Public Health Center, said this during a television broadcast, according to an Ukrinform correspondent. “In Ukraine, dozens of hantavirus infection cases are recorded annually, but this hantavirus is transmitted exclusively from rodents to humans,” Hanich said. He explained that infection can occur through dust, contaminated surfaces, or food exposed to animal excretions. To reduce the risk of infection, people are advised not to sweep areas where rodents may be present, as this can stir contaminated dust into the air. Instead, wet cleaning with disinfectants and the use of gloves are recommended, the Public Health Center spokesperson said. Read also: New rehabilitation center for soldiers opens in Kyiv As reported by Ukrinform, an outbreak of hantavirus occurred aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius in the Atlantic Ocean, leaving three people dead. According to the vessel’s itinerary published on its website, the MV Hondius departed from Ushuaia in southern Argentina on March 20 and was scheduled to complete its voyage in Cape Verde on May 4. South African Health Ministry spokesperson Foster Mohale said there were about 150 tourists from various countries on board the vessel. Two passengers aboard the Hondius cruise ship were officially diagnosed with hantavirus after being evacuated to the Netherlands. A Swiss citizen who had traveled to South America on the cruise ship affected by the hantavirus outbreak tested positive for the virus after returning home and is currently undergoing treatment. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry stated that five Ukrainian citizens are among the crew members of the MV Hondius, and there have been no signs of deterioration in their health. On May 10, the MV Hondius arrived at the port of Tenerife in Spain. analysis.time: Ukraine records dozens of hantavirus cases each year, with the outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship occurring between March 20 and May 4, 2026, and the ship arriving in Tenerife on May 10, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred on the MV Hondius cruise ship, which traveled from Ushuaia, Argentina, to Cape Verde, with stops in Spain. The affected population included 150 tourists from various countries and five Ukrainian citizens among the crew.
analysis.event: An outbreak of hantavirus was reported on the MV Hondius cruise ship, resulting in three deaths and two confirmed cases. The Public Health Center of Ukraine confirmed that hantavirus is transmitted exclusively from rodents to humans.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Three people died, and two were officially diagnosed with hantavirus. The virus spreads through dust, contaminated surfaces, or food exposed to rodent excretions. The Public Health Center advised against sweeping to avoid stirring up contaminated dust.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Public Health Center of Ukraine provided guidance on prevention, recommending wet cleaning with disinfectants and the use of gloves. The Ukrainian Foreign Ministry reported no health deterioration among the five Ukrainian crew members.

analysis.brief_en: Ukraine's Public Health Center confirmed that dozens of hantavirus infection cases are recorded annually, with the virus transmitted exclusively from rodents to humans. An outbreak of hantavirus occurred on the MV Hondius cruise ship, which traveled from Ushuaia, Argentina, to Cape Verde, resulting in three deaths and two confirmed cases. The ship arrived in Tenerife, Spain, on May 10, 2026. The Public Health Center advised against sweeping to avoid stirring up contaminated dust and recommended wet cleaning with disinfectants and the use of gloves. Five Ukrainian citizens were among the crew, and no health deterioration was reported for them. The outbreak highlights the importance of rodent prevention measures, especially in enclosed spaces like cruise ships.

news.content: HeadTopics TopLatestStoriesVideosGamesPoliticsSportsBusinessCrime WHO chief urges completion of international pandemic treaty amid Ebola and hantavirus threats NG TopPoliticsSportsBusinessCrimeEducationHealthEconomyEntertainmentTechnology Advertisement Discover more Track Outbreaks Find Global Grants Check Symptoms Study Biology Get Health Tips Read Health News News aggregation platform Health WHO chief urges completion of international pandemic treaty amid Ebola and hantavirus threats channelstv#7 in Nigeria02/11/2026 16:13:00 2 min read WHO · Pandemic Treaty · Ebola Advertisement World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has called on nations to finalize an international pandemic treaty, citing ongoing Ebola and hantavirus outbreaks as urgent reminders that no country can protect itself from pandemics alone. Share on WhatsApp In this file photo taken on March 11, 2020 shows World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus attending a press briefing on COVID-19 at the WHO headquarters in Geneva. TrackOutbreaks The World Health Organization chief said late November 1, 2020, that he was self-quarantining after someone he had been in contact with tested positive for Covid-19, but stressed he had no symptoms. Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday. TrackOutbreaks Also readNigeria reports two new suspected Ebola cases in North-east, NCDC says Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice. As the ninth meeting towards finalizing the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to “finish the job”. Discover more Political news analysis Local news publishing News “A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country,” he said, according to a written version of his statement. “The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat. TrackOutbreaks Advertisement ”He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC. It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: “no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone”. TrackOutbreaks Discover more Breaking news alerts Nigeria news updates Headline news service When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line. The agreement’s Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments. During the Covid pandemic, he highlighted that “the world developed vaccines in record time, but too many countries were left waiting while others secured far more than they needed”. Completing the final piece of the pandemic treaty, he insisted, was “the key that will unlock the door to a safer future”. channelstv#7 in Nigeria We have summarized this news so that you can read it quickly. analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, has called for the completion of an international pandemic treaty, emphasizing the urgent need for global cooperation in light of ongoing threats like the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April 2026. The treaty, which was adopted last year as a framework for handling future pandemics, includes a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system to ensure equitable access to vaccines, tests, and treatments. However, disagreements persist between wealthy and developing nations over its implementation. Nigeria recently reported two suspected Ebola cases in the North-East, both of which are under investigation and isolated for testing. The WHO chief stressed that no country can protect itself from pandemics alone, citing the global impact of the Covid-19 pandemic as a key lesson. The treaty's finalization is seen as critical to creating a safer future for global health.

news.title_zh: 世卫组织总干事敦促在埃博拉和汉坦病毒威胁下完成国际大流行病条约 - Head Topics
news.source_body_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, has called for the completion of an international pandemic treaty, emphasizing the urgent need for global cooperation in light of ongoing threats like the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April 2026. The treaty, which was adopted last year as a framework for handling future pandemics, includes a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system to ensure equitable access to vaccines, tests, and treatments. However, disagreements persist between wealthy and developing nations over its implementation. Nigeria recently reported two suspected Ebola cases in the North-East, both of which are under investigation and isolated for testing. The WHO chief stressed that no country can protect itself from pandemics alone, citing the global impact of the Covid-19 pandemic as a key lesson. The treaty's finalization is seen as critical to creating a safer future for global health.
news.content_zh: 世界卫生组织 (WHO) 总干事谭德塞呼吁完成一项国际大流行病条约,强调鉴于刚果民主共和国埃博拉疫情和 2026 年 4 月导致游轮上三人死亡的汉坦病毒暴发 等持续威胁,迫切需要开展全球合作。该条约于去年通过,作为应对未来大流行病的框架,其中包括病原体准入利益分享系统,以确保公平地获得 疫苗、测试和 治疗。然而,富裕国家和发展中国家之间对其实施仍存在分歧。尼日利亚近期报告东北部出现两例埃博拉疑似病例,两例均正在接受调查和隔离检测。世卫组织总干事强调,没有一个国家能够单独保护自己免受流行病的侵害,并指出 Covid-19 大流行的全球影响是一个重要的教训。该条约的最终确定对于为全球健康创造更安全的未来至关重要。

In April 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus infection, caused by the Andes virus, was detected on board the Dutch cruise ship M/V Hondius. The ship departed from the Argentine port of Ushuaia on April 1, 2026. A total of three people on board died. According to the World Health Organization, nine probable and seven confirmed cases of hantavirus infection have been recorded. On May 10, passengers began disembarking in Tenerife, Canary Islands, and were transported home on charter flights. Eighteen people are under medical observation in the United States due to possible infection—17 American citizens and one British-American citizen. Sixteen of them are being treated at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, and two have been transferred to Emory University in Atlanta. Passengers who test negative will be monitored for 42 days. As events unfolded, social media users noted similarities to a 2012 episode of “The Simpsons”, which also featured a virus-ridden cruise ship. The show's creators had previously been credited with "predicting" Donald Trump's presidential victory in a 2000 episode and the rise of smartwatches and video calls in a 1995 episode. US officials stress that the risk to the general public remains extremely low. Poster Pop singers will perform in Ashgabat. news.source_body_en: In April 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus infection caused by the Andes virus was detected on the Dutch cruise ship M/V Hondius, which had departed from the Argentine port of Ushuaia on April 1. The World Health Organization confirmed nine probable and seven confirmed cases, with three deaths reported. Passengers began disembarking in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on May 10, and were transported home on charter flights. Eighteen individuals, including 17 American citizens and one British-American citizen, are under medical observation in the United States. Sixteen of these are being treated at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, while two have been transferred to Emory University in Atlanta. The outbreak has prompted monitoring of those who test negative for 42 days. US officials have stated that the risk to the general public remains extremely low. The event has been linked to a 2012 episode of «The Simpsons», which featured a virus-ridden cruise ship, sparking claims of its predictive nature.

news.content_title: Study Identifies How Antibodies Block Hantavirus Entry
news.content: SCIENTISTS have revealed how New World hantaviruses recognise a human cell receptor, providing structural insights that could support the development of future antiviral treatments. Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that can cause severe disease in humans, yet no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained unclear. The study, published in Nature, describes the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution, clarifying how the virus engages its receptor. Revealing the Receptor-Binding Mechanism The researchers found that PCDH1 binds asymmetrically within a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the viral spike. This recessed binding site helps explain why PCDH1 recognises only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers, rather than isolated components. The findings identify a structural strategy through which hantaviruses can conceal their receptor-binding site within a depression on the viral surface. Understanding this arrangement provides insight into how the virus establishes the interaction needed for cell entry. Viral Loops Shape Recognition Mutagenesis experiments identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site. The researchers also demonstrated that these structural features can enable PCDH1 binding to be transferred from New World to Old World hantavirus glycoproteins. These findings help define the viral features responsible for receptor recognition and offer a clearer understanding of the structural determinants governing interactions between hantaviruses and host cells. Antibodies Block Hantavirus Entry Structural and functional analyses of four neutralising antibodies revealed two distinct mechanisms for blocking receptor binding. Some antibodies occluded access to the PCDH1-binding site, while others prevented receptor engagement through steric interference. Together, these results explain how antibodies can counter the virus’s recessed receptor-binding strategy. The structural framework established by the study could inform the design of antiviral therapeutics that target the hantavirus spike, addressing an important gap in treatment options for these potentially severe infections. Although the findings provide a foundation for future therapeutic development, further work will be needed to translate these structural insights into effective treatments. Reference Battini L et al. Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses. Nature. 2026. [Epub ahead of print]

news.content_zh: 2026年《自然》杂志发表的一项研究揭示了新世界汉坦病毒(包括安第斯病毒(ANDV))如何识别人类细胞受体原钙粘蛋白-1(PCDH1)进入宿主细胞的结构基础。科学家利用结构和功能分析证明,PCDH1 在由病毒刺突中的四个 Gn 原聚体形成的深中央口袋内不对称结合。这一发现解释了为什么 PCDH1 只识别完整的病毒颗粒或可溶性四聚体,而不是分离的成分。该研究还确定了抗体阻止汉坦病毒进入的两种不同机制:阻断 PCDH1 结合位点的进入和通过空间干扰阻止受体结合。这些结果为开发针对汉坦病毒尖峰的 抗病毒药物 疗法奠定了基础,解决了针对这些潜在严重感染的 治疗 选择中的关键差距。然而,需要进一步的工作将这些结构见解转化为有效的 治疗。

Upon arrival, all on board will undergo a medical examination, receive the necessary care, and be repatriated. news.content_title: Five regions of the Russian Federation are suffering from a mouse infestation
news.content: News War with the russian federation Five regions of the Russian Federation are suffering from a mouse infestation UA NEWS 02 November 2026 21:42 In 2026, a sharp increase in the incidence of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), also known as “mouse fever,” was recorded in a number of Russian regions. According to the data provided, in the Nizhny Novgorod and Saratov regions, as well as in Tatarstan, Bashkortostan, and Udmurtia, a diagnosis of “mouse fever” in at least 1,512 patients, of whom 656 cases were in Udmurtia, 367 in Bashkortostan, and 278 in the Nizhny Novgorod region—a figure 2.2 times higher than the long-term average. The causative agent of this acute infectious disease is the hantavirus, which is carried by rodents (particularly field mice and gray rats). news.source_body_en: In November 2026, a sharp increase in the incidence of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), also known as 'mouse fever,' was reported in five regions of the Russian Federation, including Nizhny Novgorod, Saratov, Tatarstan, Bashkortostan, and Udmurtia. The disease is caused by the hantavirus, which is carried by rodents such as field mice and gray rats. The infection spreads to humans through airborne dust, contaminated food, or broken skin, leading to symptoms like high fever, kidney damage, and systemic toxicity. news.content_zh: 2026年11月,俄罗斯联邦下诺夫哥罗德、萨拉托夫、鞑靼斯坦、巴什科尔托斯坦和乌德穆尔特等五个地区报告了肾综合征出血热(HFRS)的发病率(也称为“老鼠热”)急剧增加。这种疾病是由田鼠和灰鼠等啮齿类动物携带的汉坦病毒病毒引起的。总共记录了至少 1,512 例病例,其中乌德穆尔特共和国病例数最多(656 例),其次是巴什科尔托斯坦共和国(367 例)和下诺夫哥罗德(278 例)。这种感染通过空气中的灰尘、受污染的食物或破损的皮肤传播给人类,导致高烧、肾脏损伤和全身中毒等症状。专家将病例激增归因于啮齿动物数量增加及其季节性迁徙到居民区,尽管该病毒不会在人与人之间传播。目前情况仍在调查中,没有证据表明 传播 存在人传人现象。
